rows.sentence: Based on `doc.txt`, here is what the document says about VBAC (vaginal birth after cesarean):
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The introduction correctly expands the abbreviation VBAC.

rows.sentence: Faster recovery and shorter hospital stay.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists both as benefits of VBAC compared with a C-section.

rows.sentence: No abdominal surgery.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly lists avoiding abdominal surgery as a benefit.

rows.sentence: Avoiding or lowering C-section risks like heavy bleeding and infection.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists heavy bleeding and infection as C-section risks that VBAC may avoid or lower.

rows.sentence: Vaginal birth helps clear amniotic fluid from your baby's lungs as it passes through the birth canal.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly describes this effect of passing through the birth canal.

rows.sentence: This better prepares your baby to breathe oxygen after birth.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly links clearing amniotic fluid with better preparation for breathing after birth.

rows.sentence: Your baby gets an immune system boost as it travels through the birth canal during a vaginal delivery.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context states this benefit directly.

rows.sentence: Less risk of complications from repeat surgeries like scarring or injuries to nearby organs.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists a lower risk of repeat-surgery complications and gives both examples.

rows.sentence: Personal preference.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly identifies personal preference as a reason to choose VBAC.

rows.sentence: Some people want the experience of a vaginal birth.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context expressly gives this as an example of personal preference.

rows.sentence: Because a C-section leaves a scar on your uterus, the pressure of labor could cause your uterus to open (rupture) along your C-section scar.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly says labor pressure could cause the uterus to rupture along the scar.

rows.sentence: Although rare, a uterine rupture is a serious complication that can have life-threatening results.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context describes uterine rupture as rare, serious, and potentially life-threatening.

rows.sentence: Other risks of attempting a VBAC are: Blood loss.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists blood loss among the risks of attempting a VBAC.

rows.sentence: Infection.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists infection among the risks of attempting a VBAC.

rows.sentence: Emergency C-section (which is riskier than a planned C-section).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists emergency C-section as a risk and says it is riskier than a planned C-section.

rows.sentence: The risk of uterine rupture if you've had a C-section with a transverse cut (sideways across the lower part of the uterus) is about 0.9% or slightly less than 1 in 100.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives the same incision description and risk estimate.

rows.sentence: The type of incision matters: "A low transverse incision has the lowest risk of uterine rupture," "A low vertical incision (up and down cut) has a higher risk of rupture than a low transverse incision," and "A high vertical incision ('classical' incision) in the upper part of your uterus has the highest risk of uterine rupture."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context confirms all three comparisons of rupture risk by incision type.

rows.sentence: Studies show that up to 75% of people who had one C-section went on to have a successful vaginal birth in their next pregnancy.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context reports the same upper estimate for the next pregnancy after one C-section.

rows.sentence: But your chance of having a successful VBAC drops to about 50% if you've had two or more prior C-section deliveries.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives the same approximate success rate after two or more prior C-sections.

rows.sentence: Your chances of having a successful VBAC may be higher if you: Have had previous C-section deliveries (one or two) with low transverse incisions.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context identifies one or two prior C-sections with low transverse incisions as a factor that may favor success.

rows.sentence: Have had a vaginal birth before.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists prior vaginal birth as a factor that may increase the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Haven't had any other uterine surgeries (such as fibroid removal, also called myomectomy).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists having no other uterine surgeries as a favorable factor and gives the same example.

rows.sentence: Have no history of uterine rupture.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists no history of uterine rupture as a favorable factor.

rows.sentence: Don't have a medical condition (like fibroids or problems with the location of your placenta) that makes a vaginal delivery risky.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists the absence of conditions that make vaginal delivery risky and includes both examples.

rows.sentence: Go into labor on your own before your due date.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists spontaneous labor before the due date as a factor that may favor success.

rows.sentence: Also: "If you've already had a successful VBAC — without complications such as ruptured uterus — you're more likely to have successful future vaginal deliveries."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context links a prior uncomplicated VBAC with a greater likelihood of successful future vaginal deliveries.

rows.sentence: Your chances of having a successful VBAC may be lower if you: Had a prior C-section due to labor not progressing...
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists a prior C-section for labor that did not progress as a factor that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Are older than 35.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists being older than 35 as a factor that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Have obesity or overweight.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists obesity or overweight as a factor that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Are giving birth to a large fetus or expecting multiples.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists both a large fetus and expecting multiples as factors that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Are past your due date.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists being past the due date as a factor that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Had a baby within the last 18 months (short time between pregnancies).
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context gives the same 18-month interval and identifies it as a factor that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: Have preeclampsia.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context lists preeclampsia as a factor that may lower the chance of success.

rows.sentence: (Healthcare providers may prefer a C-section delivery.)
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context explicitly makes this qualification in its entry on preeclampsia.

rows.sentence: One note: the document lists these factors as things that may raise or lower your chances, but it does not frame them as criteria you can "work towards" or give guidance on which are within your control.
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The success-factor lists describe circumstances associated with higher or lower chances, not goals to work toward, and do not distinguish which factors a person can control.

rows.sentence: It does advise that "When you talk about how safe VBAC is with your provider, make sure they look at your medical records and the reasons for any C-sections you've had," and suggests discussing with your provider topics including "Past pregnancies and deliveries," "Reason(s) you had a C-section," "Safety of VBAC and a repeat C-section for you and your baby," "A plan for inducing labor (or not)," and "If the healthcare facility can manage emergency deliveries."
rows.label: supported
rows.rationale: The context recommends reviewing medical records and prior C-section reasons, and it lists all five discussion topics named in the sentence.
